name: ACME Academy
summary: A multi-branch education group: corporate offices in Ankara, İstanbul and London plus a campus of ~10,000 students. The design segments staff, students, R&D and software onto separate VLANs, exposes public services only through a DMZ, and reaches branches over a role-based VPN. This is a worked seed — copy its shape, not its numbers.

vlans.note: R&D lab; no direct internet, egress via proxy.

vlans.note: Firewall, switch and iDRAC management; VPN only.

alternatives.reason: Cheaper and fast, but IPS/UTM and support are weaker for a regulated org.
Open and auditable; smaller ecosystem for staff already trained on FortiOS.
Strong UTM and reporting; licensing cost grows with add-ons.
Best app-ID, but throughput with threat prevention is tight at the edge for this link.

vlans.name: students-wifi
vlans.note: ~16k addresses: students carry 2–3 devices each, so the /24-per-person rule of thumb does not apply — size by devices.

chosen.reason: 10 Gbps campus link with IPS on at exam peaks; NGFW throughput has real headroom unlike a 440 at this load.

alternatives.reason: Best policy engine; threat-prevention throughput is short of a 10 Gbps peak.
Great raw price/throughput; UTM and support thinner for a campus SOC.
Strong UTM and reporting; licence add-ons raise TCO.
Excellent management at scale; highest cost here.

Rate-limit at the edge; exam-day traffic looks like a flood otherwise.
NTP.
DHCP for student Wi-Fi — the one service you must never firewall off internally.
Student Wi-Fi is isolated from faculty/admin.
No student device reaches network management.

remoteAccess.note: No public SSH anywhere. Admins reach the management VLANs through a role-based VPN into a bastion; staff get a separate profile with only the apps their role needs. Each branch terminates its own tunnel to HQ.

monitoring.siem: Wazuh + the ufw-logger Telegram notifier for quick block alerts
monitoring.owner: Campus SOC (2 analysts) owns security alerts; branch IT owns uptime. An alert nobody owns is an alert nobody answers.
monitoring.alertSink: SIEM dashboard for triage; Telegram channel for high-severity blocks only (the logger is profiled to drop outbound ALLOW and DNS noise so it never floods).
monitoring.appVsSecurity: Application health (ERP, LMS up/down) goes to the ops channel; security events (blocks, auth failures, IPS hits) go to the SOC. Mixing them buries the ones that matter.

cveWatch.note: Portal runs PHP-FPM on Linux; verified version and confirmed the CGI path is not used. Firewall is the wrong layer for an app-layer RCE — mitigation is WAF + patch.
